Source-row extraction relies on normal UTF-8 Markdown and documented .NET string behavior.
SHA-256/Git checkout/runner can theoretically fail outside documented behavior.
The source is Markdown with a reviewed bounded table shape. Intentional source schema changes fail closed and require adapter/manifest review rather than heuristic recovery.
`loc.*` / `fam.*` are the accepted identity families currently present. A future new family will fail closed until the query contract deliberately adopts it.
District strings are source labels, not a newly canonical district ontology.
RD-1..RD-4 cannot be honestly measured without realized traversal/runtime evidence and are deliberately not inferred.

**Future PA evolution.** A new PA or an intentional revision of PA-01..05 may require a new entity/field/relation shape. DW-03 deliberately fails closed rather than pretending v1 is universal.

**Unstructured narrative.** Prose outside `SOURCE_MANIFEST_V1.md` is not first-class query data in v1. It remains authoritative and source-open through provenance; DW-03 does not claim the compact corpus substitutes for rereading source when a consumer needs material outside the declared suite.

**Same-authority navigation is not proof attribution.** `same-authority-evidence` and `same-authority-fixture` make accepted material reachable; they do not assert that every evidence row or fixture individually proves every finding.
**Trusted primitives.** Git blob identity, cryptographic hashes, filesystem/source reads and inherited Design World normalization are trusted infrastructure.
**No context-efficiency claim.** The existence of a compact deterministic index does not prove token savings, model quality or optimal agent retrieval. Those measurements belong to DW-04.
**No runtime claim.** Research fixtures and projected PA semantics do not prove Unity/runtime implementation, persistence, performance or final H0 architecture.

**Single reviewed v1 domain.** The current accepted corpus has one projected domain, `living-world`. `ByDomain` is exact for that reviewed universe and returns empty for unknown domains; a future second domain requires explicit reviewed extension rather than implicit classification.
Provider token/cost observations remain diagnostic only; no universal token- or cost-saving claim is accepted.
